pathways.climate_pressure: Changing rainfall and environmental stress affecting grazing and water resources.
pathways.documented_impact: DPPA describes altered transhumance and pressure around refugee-hosting areas outside Mbera.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Longstanding resentments, grazing competition and unequal representation/access among arrival cohorts.
pathways.possible_consequence: Potential host–refugee or inter-herder tensions; no climate-attributable violence incidence is estimated.
alternative_explanations: Historical resentments, representation, services and insecurity in neighbouring Mali also shape pressures.
pathways.uncertainty: Source-stated conditional pathway in an executive summary; underlying incident evidence not reviewed, not proof that climate caused armed violence.
resilience_factors: Communal committees and inclusive resource governance are identified capacities, with effectiveness unverified.
pathways.compact_statement: Around Mbera, climate-related resource pressure can interact with longstanding grievances and grazing/water access; tensions are conditional, not inevitable.

gaps: Main inspected the three-page DPPA executive summary and other primary publications. Cohort representation, longstanding resentments and resource governance mediate risks; refugee presence is not itself a violence predictor.
The UNICEF composite is a child climate-risk measure, not an FCV classification; the report's dated baselines and historical assistance figures are retained.

executive_assessment.text: Child-risk mapping differentiates six high-risk wilayas, while Hodh El Chargui and Mbera-area evidence adds drought, displacement and service/resource pressures.
DPPA identifies mediated grazing/water and transhumance tensions, alongside committees and policy capacities; these are qualitative pathways, not national causal estimates.
